The database schema named 'rschema_0431' consists of six tables: User, Department, Doctor, Appointment, Schedule, and History.
The User table contains Contact_Information, Password, User_ID, and Username columns. User_ID is the primary key of this table, ensuring entity integrity as it is unique and not null.
The Department table has Department_ID, Department_Name, and Introduction columns. Department_ID is the primary key of this table, ensuring entity integrity.
The Doctor table has Doctor_ID, Doctor_Name, Title, and Department_ID columns. Doctor_ID is the primary key of this table, ensuring entity integrity. Department_ID is a foreign key referencing the Department table, ensuring referential integrity.
The Appointment table contains Appointment_ID, Appointment_Time, Doctor_ID, Status, and User_ID columns. Appointment_ID is the primary key of this table, ensuring entity integrity. Doctor_ID and User_ID are foreign keys referencing the Doctor and User tables, respectively, ensuring referential integrity.
The Schedule table contains Date, Doctor_ID, Remaining_Appointments, Schedule_ID, and Time_Slot columns. Doctor_ID is a foreign key referencing the Doctor table, ensuring referential integrity.
Finally, the History table contains Appointment_ID, History_ID, Operation_Time, Operation_Type, and User_ID columns. Appointment_ID and User_ID are foreign keys referencing the Appointment and User tables, respectively, ensuring referential integrity.
This schema is designed to manage a medical appointment system, with tables representing users, departments, doctors, appointments, schedules, and operation histories. The tables are interconnected through foreign keys, ensuring data integrity and consistency.
gold_question:
The main functional requirements for the hospital appointment registration system are described as follows:
Design and implement a hospital appointment registration management system.
The system shall support displaying hospital department information (including department name, introduction, department doctors, etc.).
The system shall support querying doctor scheduling information (providing doctor name, department, consultation time, remaining appointments, etc.).
The system shall support online appointment registration (users can select doctor and appointment time), canceling appointments, and querying historical records (including registered and canceled appointment records).
The system shall support user information management (storing username, password, contact information, etc.), system management (administrators can maintain doctor information, department information, appointment records, etc.).
The system shall support statistical analysis (perform statistics and analysis on appointment status to provide decision support for the hospital). 
The system shall ensure data security (adopt various measures to protect user information and data security).
The system shall optimize hospital service efficiency and user experience.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0431
CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `username` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `contact_information` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `department` (
  `department_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `department_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `introduction` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`department_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `doctor` (
  `doctor_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `doctor_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `department_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`doctor_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `doctor_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`department_id`) REFERENCES `department` (`department_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `appointment` (
  `appointment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `appointment_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `doctor_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `status` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`appointment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `appointment_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`doctor_id`) REFERENCES `doctor` (`doctor_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `appointment_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `schedule` (
  `schedule_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `doctor_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `date` date NOT NULL,
  `time_slot` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `remaining_appointments` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`schedule_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `schedule_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`doctor_id`) REFERENCES `doctor` (`doctor_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `history` (
  `history_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `appointment_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `operation_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `operation_type` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`history_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `history_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`appointment_id`) REFERENCES `appointment` (`appointment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `history_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
